source.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
source.authors: Dominik Meier; Luca Joshua Francis; Marco Bernhard Kaiser; T. Ruas; Jan Philip Wahle; B. Gipp

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses single-direction refusal work, but its experiments concern following or resisting tampered reasoning traces, not refusal of harmful user requests. It neither tests nor relies on the refusal direction as a tool.
record.gate_note: The paper measures and steers residual-stream directions for resistance to unsafe reasoning and compliance with tampered reasoning. Those are related to, but distinct from, refusal as defined in the claim. The authors also compare their findings to prior work on refusal directions; they do not experimentally test refusal-direction ablation, refusal induction, abliteration, jailbreak suppression of that direction, or refusal in reasoning models.
record.test_reason: The study borrows the difference-of-means construction from Arditi et al. but applies it to a different construct. Its directions separate resisting from complying with tampered reasoning traces in an agentic multiple-choice setting, not refusing from complying with harmful user requests. It never ablates, adds or weight-edits a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. Refusal-direction work is mentioned only in comparison: 'prior work often locates refusal as a single direction'. The redundancy finding is also likened to SAE refusal work and CoT Hijacking. None of its results bear on V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also conclude that more faithful models are less safe against tampered reasoning. They add that the safety direction's redundancy lies outside the single-direction refusal-signal mechanism, while the faithfulness pathway fits it. That is an interpretive comparison, not a test of the refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not test the original refusal-direction recipe. It uses difference-of-means probes for reasoning-manipulation outcomes and adds those directions at L44; it does not ablate a refusal direction across layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported directions peak at L44 attention output and the steering results vary with direction and alpha. The paper also reports different baselines and steering effects when TRR uses LLM-based coherent replacements rather than search-and-replace.

fits_no_version.finding: In the joint (α_safe, α_faith) sweep, the best safety cell (+5,+1; 0.95) and best faithfulness cell (−3,+5; 0.71) sit in opposite corners. At (+5,+5), Safe Reasoning is 0.94 rather than the 0.85 baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In QwQ-32B, resistance to and compliance with tampered reasoning span a 2D steering subspace rather than one signed axis.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention-mask ablation at L45–L63 shows two pathways for v_safe: direction alone 0.79, mask alone 0.80, combined 0.87. For v_faith, the mask drops faithfulness 13–17 pp below baseline whether or not the direction is applied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In QwQ-32B, resisting tampered reasoning uses redundant pathways, while following it uses a single integrated attention pathway.

fits_no_version.finding: On neutral tasks, v_safe at α=+3 shortens the median reasoning trace from 808 to 742 tokens, and v_faith at α=+3 lengthens it to 886 tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tampered-reasoning resistance and compliance directions shift reasoning length in opposite directions on untampered tasks.

record.problems: The behavioral benchmark has 77 human-crafted scenarios, which the authors say limits statistical power. Mechanistic analysis and steering were conducted only on QwQ-32B. The authors note that literal replacements can create linguistic artifacts, and that LLM-based rewrites introduce uncertainty and noise. These limitations concern the study's reasoning-manipulation findings; it has no direct evidence about refusal-direction causality.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly testing refusal-direction behavior were reported. The paper's main cross-model HazMart faithfulness and safety rates were not included because they concern responses to tampered reasoning traces rather than refusal of harmful user requests.

untested.parts: Ablating or adding a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction and its effect on refusal rates. The MMLU check (R11) concerns steering a tampered-reasoning-resistance direction, not refusal ablation.
Weight-edit or abliteration of a refusal direction.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction, and adversarial training against its ablation. CoT Hijacking is only cited.
Multi-dimensional or conical structure of refusal itself. The 2D finding concerns safety and faithfulness directions for tampered reasoning.
Separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base to instruct.
Effect of refusal training on direction existence. Fine-tuning is only proposed as future work.
The study works on reasoning models (QwQ-32B) but never extracts or ablates a refusal direction in them.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ["none"]. The attention-mask, joint-sweep and trace-length results bear on no version, so they are listed under fits_no_version, not missing. Leaving out the cross-model HazMart rates is justified. 'discusses'/T6 is kept rather than T4: the paper reuses the difference-of-means recipe, not the refusal-direction finding itself.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction causes refusal, whether removing it eliminates refusal, whether adding it induces refusal, or whether other abilities are preserved after those refusal interventions.
No weight edit or abliteration of a refusal direction is tested.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress a refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.

The study finds distinct directions for resistance to tampered reasoning and compliance with it, not for refusal; it does not test whether refusal is affine, conical, or composed of a dominant direction plus others.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
The study does not vary refusal training or test when refusal training creates a removable direction.
Although the study evaluates reasoning models, it does not test whether the refusal direction or its claimed causal effects hold in models that reason before answering.

rows.subject: QwQ-32B
rows.operation_detail: Difference-of-means direction trained on the safety condition; classifies safe choices versus choices complying with tampered unsafe reasoning.

conditions.value: held-out 5-fold cross-validation, folds disjoint by scenario

rows.measure: AUROC for safe versus unsafe-option choice
rows.note: This probes the response to manipulated reasoning, not refusal of a harmful user request.

rows.subject: QwQ-32B
rows.operation_detail: Difference-of-means direction trained on the faithfulness condition; classifies following versus resisting a safe-option swap in the reasoning trace.

conditions.value: held-out 5-fold cross-validation, folds disjoint by scenario

rows.measure: AUROC for following the tampered safe reasoning
rows.note: This measures compliance with a safe reasoning alteration, not refusal.

rows.subject: QwQ-32B
rows.operation_detail: Compared the cosine similarity of the safety and faithfulness directions.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between the two directions
rows.note: The authors describe the directions as anti-correlated but not collinear; these directions represent resistance to and compliance with tampered reasoning.

rows.subject: QwQ-32B
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonalized each direction against the other and tested prediction on its native condition.
rows.baseline: unorthogonalized direction; AUROC not stated here
rows.note: The result supports distinct information in the two directions for the study's reasoning-manipulation measures, not distinct refusal directions.

rows.subject: QwQ-32B
rows.operation_detail: Applied each direction to the other direction's condition.
rows.note: The authors say the direction anti-predicts the cross metric. The metrics concern tampered-reasoning behavior, not refusal.

rows.subject: QwQ-32B
rows.operation_detail: Added the safety direction at each generated token with per-token renormalization.
rows.measure: Safe Reasoning score on tampered unsafe reasoning
rows.note: This is steering of resistance to an unsafe reasoning alteration, not induction of refusal to a harmless request.

rows.subject: QwQ-32B
